# Gospel of Philip — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, pp. 51-86 | Coptic
**Consensus Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** A Hebrew makes a Hebrew, and such a person is called a proselyte. But a proselyte does not make a proselyte. Some simply are what they are and produce others like themselves, while others merely come into being.

**1:2** The slave seeks only his freedom, not the estate of his master. But the son is not only a son — he lays claim to the inheritance of the father.

**1:3** Those who inherit the dead are dead themselves, and they inherit dead things. Those who inherit the living are alive themselves, and they inherit both the living and the dead.

**1:4** The dead inherit nothing. How could a dead person inherit? Yet if the dead one inherits from the living, they will not die — on the contrary, they will live all the more.

**1:5** A Gentile does not die, for a Gentile has never lived so as to die. One who has believed the truth has lived — and now this person risks death, for they are truly alive.

**1:6** Since Christ came, the world was created, cities were established, and the dead were carried out for burial.

**1:7** When we were Hebrews we were orphans, with only a mother. But when we became Christians we acquired both a father and a mother.

**1:8** Those who sow in winter harvest in summer. The winter is the world; the summer is the other aeon. Let us sow in the world so that we may harvest in summer. Because of this it is not fitting to pray in winter.

**1:9** Summer comes out of winter. But one who reaps in winter only uproots — that season yields no fruit. [...] Not only [...] in this way [...] but the Sabbath too is barren.

**1:10** Christ came to ransom some, to save others, to redeem others still. He ransomed those who were strangers and claimed them as his own. He set apart those who were already his — the ones he had given as a pledge according to his will.

**1:11** It was not only when he appeared that he voluntarily laid down his life. He laid it down from the very day the world came into being. Then he came to take it back, for it had been given as a pledge. It had fallen into the hands of robbers and been taken captive — but he saved it. He redeemed both the good and the evil in the world.

**1:12** The light and the darkness, life and death, the right and the left — they are brothers of one another. It is not possible for the good to relinquish the evil, nor the evil the good, nor life death, nor death life. Because of this each will dissolve into its original nature. But those who are exalted above the world cannot dissolve — they are eternal.

**1:13** The names given to worldly things are profoundly deceptive, for they turn the heart away from what is real toward what is not real. Whoever hears the word "God" does not perceive the real thing but perceives what is not real. So also with "the Father" and "the Son" and "the Holy Spirit" and "life" and "light" and "resurrection" and "the Church" — and all the rest. People do not perceive the real but only the unreal, unless they have come to know what is truly real. Names heard in the world deceive. If they belonged to the aeon, they would not always be used as names in the world, nor assigned to worldly things. They have their end in the aeon.

**1:14** There is one single name that is not uttered in the world — the name the Father bestowed upon the Son. It is above every other name. This is the Father's own name: the Son would not have become the Father had he not clothed himself in the name of the Father. Those who possess this name know it but do not speak it. Those who do not possess it do not know it.

**1:15** But truth brought names into being in the world for our sake, because it is not possible to teach truth without names. Truth is one — and also many — and for our sake it teaches this one thing through the many.

**1:16** The archons wanted to deceive mankind, seeing that mankind had kinship with what is truly good. They took the names of the good and fastened them to the not-good, so that through names they might deceive people and bind them to what is not good. And what an irony: they thereby did mankind a service — they caused people to leave the free things and seize what is enslaved.

**1:17** A farmer cannot do his work without [...] water. So also it is impossible to build anything without water and fire [...]. The farmer reaps because of water and earth.

**1:18** God is a dyer. Just as good dyes — the kind called "true" — dissolve together with the things dyed in them, so it is with those whom God has dyed. Since his dyes are immortal, they become immortal through his colors. God dips those he dips in water.

**1:19** It is not possible for anyone to perceive anything of what truly exists unless they become like it. In the world it is not so — a person sees the sun without becoming the sun, and sees the heaven and the earth and all other things without becoming them. But in the truth it is different. You saw something of that place, and you became those things. You saw the Spirit — you became spirit. You saw Christ — you became Christ. You saw the Father — you shall become the Father. In this world you see everything but do not see yourself. In that place you will see yourself — for you shall become what you see.

**1:20** Faith receives; love gives. No one can receive without faith. No one can give without love. So in order to truly receive, we believe. And in order to truly give — for one who gives nothing has nothing — we love.

**1:21** Before Christ came, there was no bread in the world. In paradise — the place where Adam was — there were many trees and food for animals, but no wheat for human beings. Mankind fed as the animals did. But when Christ, the perfect man, came, he brought bread down from heaven so that humanity could be nourished with human food.

**1:22** The archons thought it was by their own power and will that they did what they did. But the Holy Spirit was secretly accomplishing everything through them according to its own will.

**1:23** Truth, which existed from the beginning, is sown everywhere. Many see it being sown; few are those who see it being reaped.

**1:24** Some say, "Mary was conceived by the Holy Spirit." They are in error. They do not know what they are saying. When has a woman ever been conceived by a woman? Mary is the virgin whom no power defiled. She is a great anathema to the Hebrew apostles and to the apostolic men. This virgin whom no power defiled — [...] the powers defile themselves.

**1:25** The Lord would not have said, "My Father who is in heaven," unless he had another father. He would simply have said, "My Father."

**1:26** The Lord said to the disciples [...]: "Go into every house and bring what belongs to you from there. Bring what is of the Father's house — but do not take or carry away anything."

**1:27** "Jesus" is a hidden name; "Christ" is a revealed name. For this reason "Jesus" does not exist in any other language — it is always "Jesus" wherever he is named. "Christ" in Syriac and Greek is also "Messiah" in every other language. "The Nazarene" is the revealed form of the hidden name.

**1:28** Baptism is "the holy" and is the highest of the rites; redemption is "the holy of holies"; the bridal chamber is the holiest of all — the innermost place.

**1:29** Baptism includes resurrection and redemption; redemption is within the bridal chamber. But the bridal chamber is within something that surpasses [...]. You will not find [...] there.

**1:30** Those who pray for Jerusalem love Jerusalem. Jerusalem is the vision of peace. Jerusalem gazes upon Jerusalem. The righteous love Jerusalem.

**1:31** Those who are truly holy shall be nourished by truth. [...] Some of them [...] the beasts [...].

**1:32** In this world those who put on garments are greater than the garments. In the kingdom of heaven, the garments are greater than those who have put them on.

**1:33** The whole of existence will be purified through water and fire — the visible through what is visible, and the hidden through what is hidden. Some things are hidden within visible things. There is water within water; there is fire within the chrism.

**1:34** Jesus approached them all by stealth. He did not reveal himself as he truly was, but in whatever manner they were able to see him. He revealed himself to all: to the great, as great; to the small, as small; to the angels, as an angel; to people, as a person. Because of this his Word remained hidden from everyone. Some who looked at him thought they were seeing themselves. But when he appeared to his disciples in glory on the mountain, he was not small — he had become great. And he made the disciples great so that they could see him in his greatness.

**1:35** He said on that day in the prayer of thanksgiving: "You who have joined the perfect light with the Holy Spirit — unite us with the angels as well." Do not despise the lamb, for without it one cannot see the king.

**1:36** No one can go before the king while naked. The one from heaven must be clothed — clothed in the light.

**1:37** Water and fire and light and the Holy Spirit are four powers. The perfect man makes use of all of them — for purification and for vivification. The [...] of the bridal chamber [...] by fire and light.

**1:38** The Holy Spirit breathes through everyone. The powers [...] those beneath their power [...].

**1:39** The archons do not know where one who truly understands comes from, for he does not wish them to know, lest they trouble him. Will he not then reveal himself when he is seen?

**1:40** The cup of prayer contains wine and water. It serves as a type of the blood for which thanks is given. It is filled with the Holy Spirit and belongs entirely to the perfect man. When we drink from it, we receive the perfect man.

**1:41** The living water is a body. It is fitting for us to clothe ourselves in the living man. When someone comes to go down into the water, they strip and say: "I go down so that I may receive."

**1:42** A horse sires a horse, a man begets a man, a god brings forth a god. The bridegroom and the bride — so it is. [...] No Jew [...] from a Jew comes a Jew. Such also is Christian descent.

**1:43** Those who say they will die first and then rise are in error. If they do not first receive the resurrection while they are alive, they will receive nothing when they die. So also when they speak of baptism: "Baptism is a great thing — whoever receives it will live."

**1:44** Philip the apostle said: "Joseph the carpenter planted a garden because he needed wood for his craft. He made the cross from the very trees he had planted. His own offspring hung on what he had planted. His offspring was Jesus, and the planting was the cross. But the tree of life stands at the center of paradise, and from the olive tree came the chrism, and from the chrism the resurrection."

**1:45** This world is a corpse-eater. Everything that is eaten within it is already dead. But truth is a life-eater. Therefore no one nourished by truth will die. Jesus came from that other place and brought food. To those who wished it, he gave life so that they might not die.

**1:46** God planted a garden. A man lived in the garden [...] not many trees [...] but an abundance of trees, and neither animal food nor the fruit of [...] what [...] I desired. But I [...] what they wished [...] This was the garden of God [...] and it gives life.

**1:47** I ate from [...] that place [...] a man of God [...] killed animals [...]. He prepared animal food there. But when he prepared animal food, [...] he satisfied the animals, [...] but left the people impoverished. [...] God [...] man [...].

**1:48** It was the will of God that people should eat and animals should not. When Adam ate, the animals ate too. Eating from the tree — the tree of the knowledge of good and evil — they brought death upon themselves and upon the animals.

**1:49** The Eucharist is Jesus. For in Hebrew he is called Pharisath — meaning "the one spread out" — because Jesus came to crucify the world.

**1:50** The Lord went into the dye works of Levi. He took seventy-two colors and threw them into the vat. He brought them all out white. And he said: "Even so has the Son of Man come — as a dyer."

**1:51** The Wisdom who is called "barren" is the mother of the angels. And the companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. [...] loved her more than all the disciples and used to kiss her often on the [...]. The rest of the disciples were troubled and expressed their disapproval. They said to him: "Why do you love her more than all of us?" The Savior answered and said to them: "Why do I not love you as I love her? When a blind man and one who sees stand together in darkness, there is no difference between them. When the light comes, the one who sees will see the light, and the one who is blind will remain in the darkness."

**1:52** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who exists before coming into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**1:53** The superiority of mankind is not visible but lies in what is hidden. Because of this, a person has dominion over animals that are physically stronger — in both visible and hidden respects. This gives humanity its survival. But when a person separates from that hidden quality, the animals kill, bite, and devour.

**1:54** No great thing can emerge if the small does not first exist. Nor can what is holy exist if the visible does not first exist. Indeed, what is hidden would dissolve were it not for the interplay of the visible and the hidden.

**1:55** Water within water, fire within fire, light within light — this is the baptism of truth.

**1:56** The Lord performed everything as a mystery: a baptism, a chrism, a Eucharist, a redemption, and a bridal chamber.

**1:57** He said: "I came to make the things below like the things above, and the things outside like the things inside. I came to unite them in that one place." [...] He reveals himself through types and images.

**1:58** Those who say there is a heavenly man and one above even that are mistaken. For it is the heavenly man who is called "the one below," and the one to whom the hidden belongs is above him. It is right to say "the inner and the outer" and "what is outside the outer." This is why the Lord called destruction "the outer darkness" — there is nothing beyond it.

**1:59** He said: "My Father who is in secret — go into your chamber and close the door behind you and pray to your Father who is in secret." The one who is within all things is the fullness. There is nothing more inward. This is what they call "the uppermost."

**1:60** Before Christ, some came from a place they would no longer enter, and went to a place they would no longer leave. But Christ came. Those who had gone in, he brought out. Those who had gone out, he brought back in.

**1:61** When Eve was still within Adam, death did not exist. When she was separated from him, death came into being. If she enters into him again and he receives her to himself, death will be no more.

**1:62** "My God, my God, why, O Lord, have you forsaken me?" These words he spoke on the cross — for he had been cut off from that place.

**1:63** The Lord rose from the dead. He became as he had been — but now his body was perfected flesh. Our own flesh is imperfect. But his flesh is [...] the true flesh.

**1:64** Truth did not come into the world naked, but in types and images. The world cannot receive it otherwise. There is a rebirth and there is an image of rebirth — one must be reborn through the image. There is a resurrection and it must arise through its image. The bridal chamber and its image — one must enter truth through the image. This is the restoration.

**1:65** For those who have received it, it is necessary not only to receive the resurrection but also the Holy Spirit. "Father" and "Son" are simple names; "Holy Spirit" is a double name. For they are present everywhere — above and below, in the hidden and in the manifest. The Holy Spirit is manifest below, and in the hidden above.

**1:66** In those who are holy, the Holy Spirit is holy. The evil spirit breathes below, in what is hidden. Those who are wise and good and holy seek their power from above. They may be seen, but they are not disturbed. They are not drawn away by the lower or the higher powers when they choose to be free.

**1:67** The fear in a person does not fear the beast that is greater than itself — to the greater beast it attributes intelligence or beauty or [...].

**1:68** The slave seeks only his freedom, not the wealth of his master. But the son, the true heir, not only has the right to the father's inheritance — he claims it for himself.

**1:69** Those who inherit the dead are dead themselves and inherit dead things. Those who inherit the living are alive themselves and inherit both the living and the dead.

**1:70** The dead inherit nothing. How shall a dead person inherit? Yet when a dead person inherits from a living one, they will not die but will on the contrary live all the more.

**1:71** A pagan does not die, for a pagan has never lived in order to die. But one who has believed in the truth has lived — and now faces the real risk of death, for they are truly alive.

**1:72** Since Christ came, the world has been made, cities have been established, and the dead have been carried out.

**1:73** When I was a child I was nurtured among the great. [...] It is a good thing to be raised among the great. [...] As for the Father's estate — a child will not receive the inheritance while still a minor. The master of the estate will not give it until the child comes of age.

**1:74** So also the son must not merely remain a son — he must become the father.

**1:75** Those who receive the chrism are called "anointed." The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit — it is not fitting to call the Father "Christ," nor the Son "Christ," nor the Holy Spirit "Christ." None of these holds the name as their own. The name is given only to the one whom the Father anoints.

**1:76** [...] The Father's name is the Son. He did not conceal it — it existed. Yet the Son himself had no name before the Father gave it to him. When revealed, his name is none other than the Father.

**1:77** The Word of the Lord said to the disciples: "Eat my flesh and drink my blood." Whoever says this overturns the world. The flesh is the Word, and the blood is the Holy Spirit. Whoever has received these has food and drink and clothing.

**1:78** I take issue with those who insist the flesh will not rise — for they are wrong on both counts. You say the flesh will not rise — then tell me what will, so that we may honor you. You say the spirit in the flesh, and the light in the flesh. But the Word itself is also flesh. The Word became flesh — and it was through that flesh that the Word rose — and everything was united through the flesh and the Word.

**1:79** This resurrection does not belong to the naked soul alone. What, then, shall rise? The flesh together with the soul together with the spirit.

**1:80** The soul and the spirit came into being from water and fire and light — the child of the bridal chamber — from water, fire, and light.

**1:81** Fire is the chrism; light is that fire. I do not speak of fire without form, but of the other fire — whose form is white, whose light is beautiful, and which bestows beauty.

**1:82** Truth does not come into the world naked but in types and images. It can be received no other way. There is a resurrection and there is an image of the resurrection — one must truly be reborn through the image. The image must arise through the image. The bridal chamber and its image: one must enter truth through the image — this is the restoration.

**1:83** It is fitting for those who have received [...] not only to receive redemption but to go within. [...] Those who receive are united through the Word and they receive [...].

**1:84** Is it not right to pray both night and day? The one who receives the light [...] does not pray by day — that person is the light. The one who has received the Word [...] does not receive it merely as a gift. They [...].

**1:85** If you are [...] before the days and say [...], all who believe in him [...].

**1:86** The light serves as a model for those in this world. It was not great at first. But when it grew to its fullness, it became great — and gave to both the world and the aeon.

**1:87** Those who are clothed in the perfect light — the powers and the angels cannot see their nakedness and are unable to seize them. But this light is put on in mystery, in the union of the bridal chamber.

**1:88** If the woman had not separated from the man, she would not have died with the man. His separation was the beginning of death. Because of this Christ came to repair the separation that was from the beginning, to reunite the two — and to those who had died in the separation he gives life and unites them.

**1:89** In the bridal chamber the woman is united with her husband. Those who have been united in the bridal chamber will no longer be separated from one another. Because of this Eve separated from Adam — because she had not been united with him in the bridal chamber.

**1:90** Adam's soul came into being through a breath. His partner was given to him from the Spirit — who is [...] his mother. His soul was given to him. [...] But the soul that was given to him — it is this one that [...].

**1:91** The Word brought forth what it desired — and all that it produced, it produced in secret. But the bridal chamber produces openly. Nothing is hidden on the day of the bridal chamber. None of those who share in the bridegroom's celebration are hidden.

**1:92** Abraham [...] circumcised, in order to teach us that it is fitting to destroy the flesh of the world.

**1:93** As long as a person's inner organs remain hidden, the person is alive and well. If those organs are exposed and come out, the person dies. So also: as long as the root of evil is hidden it is strong. Once it is recognized it is destroyed. Once it is exposed it perishes. For this reason the Word says: "Already the axe is laid at the root of the trees."

**1:94** It will not merely cut — what is cut will sprout again. But the axe digs until it brings up the root. Jesus pulled up the root of the entire realm, while others had done so only partially. Let each of us dig up the root of evil within us and pull it from our hearts. When we recognize it, it will be uprooted.

**1:95** But if we remain ignorant of it, it takes root within us and produces its fruit in our hearts. It rules us. We become its slaves. It takes us captive so that we do what we do not want and fail to do what we want. It is powerful only because we have not recognized it. As long as it exists, it is at work.

**1:96** Ignorance is the mother of all evils. Ignorance leads to death. Those who come from ignorance neither existed nor exist nor will exist. [...] When truth comes, all of this will be made complete.

**1:97** When truth comes, the perfect things will be revealed, the hidden things made manifest, and the holy things declared. Truth will disclose what is hidden. It will call the elect by name, and the Father will cause them to inherit what has been prepared for them.

**1:98** From those who have something, even that will be taken. From those who have nothing, even that will be taken. This is the justice of the world.

**1:99** The Master of the universe is not merely a lord — he is the Father. A lord has no son; a father does. We call him "master" only because we have not yet come to know him.

**1:100** The Word said: "Ask and you shall receive; seek and you shall find; knock and it shall be opened to you." Let us ask so that we may receive. Let us knock at the gate of the treasury of the wedding feast.

**1:101** When we pray for the Holy Spirit, in the night and in the day, we give thanks [...].

**1:102** The Son of Man came from above. He said [...]. He humbled himself to the point of death. When he had died and risen, those who [...] knew him. So it became possible for the perfect ones to be made manifest in the darkness.

**1:103** The holy man is entirely holy, including his body. If he receives bread, he sanctifies it; if he receives a cup, or anything else — he purifies those as well.

**1:104** And how shall he not also purify his body?

**1:105** As Jesus perfected the water of baptism, so he expelled death. Because of this we go down into the water but not into death, so that we are not poured out into the spirit of the world.

**1:106** When that wind blows, winter comes. When the Holy Spirit breathes, summer arrives.

**1:107** Whoever knows the truth is free, and the free person does not sin, for "the one who sins is the slave of sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father. Those the world considers beyond sin are called "free" by the world. But the knowledge of truth merely lifts up their hearts — it makes them think themselves free without making them truly aware of their own hearts.

**1:108** Love builds up. Whoever has been made free through knowledge becomes a servant on account of love — for the sake of those who have not yet attained the freedom of knowledge. Knowledge makes them capable of becoming free.

**1:109** Love never calls anything its own — yet [...] everything belongs to love. It does not say "this is mine" or "that is mine" but "all of this is yours."

**1:110** Spiritual love is wine and fragrance. All who anoint themselves with it take pleasure in it. While those who are anointed stand nearby, others who stand with them also share the fragrance. If those who are anointed leave, those who are merely nearby — but not anointed — remain with a bad smell. The Samaritan gave the wounded man nothing but wine and oil — nothing, that is, but the chrism. And it healed the wounds.

**1:111** "Love covers a multitude of sins." Love does not cover sin. What love does is make many sins invisible.

**1:112** The light that was joined to the darkness did not come out of the darkness. But now it shines both in the darkness and in the light. The perfect light will shine in every place. When it is perfect, it comes to full being.

**1:113** Say "I am a Jew" — no one is moved. Say "I am a Roman" — no one is disturbed. Say "I am a Greek, a barbarian, a slave, or free" — no one is troubled. But say "I am a Christian" — and the [...] will tremble. Would that I might receive [...] this name, which [...].

**1:114** God is a devourer of human beings. Because of this, mankind is sacrificed to him. Before humanity was sacrificed, animals were being offered. But those to whom they were offered were not gods.

**1:115** Glass vessels and clay vessels are both made by fire. But if a glass vessel breaks, it can be remade — for it came into being through breath. If a clay vessel breaks, it is destroyed — for it came into being without breath.

**1:116** A donkey turning a millstone walked a hundred miles. When it was loosened it found itself in the same place. Some people travel great distances but have no destination. When evening came upon them, they found neither city nor village, neither creation nor nature, neither power nor angel. Those wretched ones had labored in vain.

**1:117** The Eucharist is Jesus. For in Hebrew he is called Pharisath — "the one who is spread out" — because Jesus came to crucify the world.

**1:118** The Lord went into the dye works of Levi. He took seventy-two colors and threw them into the vat. He brought them all out white. And he said: "Even so has the Son of Man come as a dyer."

**1:119** The Wisdom who is called "barren" is the mother of the angels. And the companion of the Savior is Mary Magdalene. The Savior loved her more than all the disciples and used to kiss her often on the [...]. The rest of the disciples were offended and expressed their disapproval. They said to him: "Why do you love her more than all of us?" The Savior answered and said: "Why do I not love you as I love her? When a blind man and one who sees stand together in darkness, there is no difference between them. When the light comes, the one who sees will see the light, and the one who is blind will remain in the darkness."

**1:120** The Lord said: "Blessed is the one who exists before coming into being. For whoever is, was, and shall be."

**1:121** The superiority of mankind is not visible but lies in what is hidden. Therefore a person masters animals that are stronger — in both visible and hidden respects. This hidden quality gives humanity its survival. But when a person separates from it, the animals slay, bite, and devour.

**1:122** The one who has come to know the truth is free. The free person does not sin. "The one who sins is the slave of sin." Truth is the mother; knowledge is the father.

**1:123** Those who are simply prevented from sinning are called "free" by the world. But the knowledge of truth only raises their hearts — which is to say, it makes them arrogant. Yet this too is a form of freedom.

**1:124** The bridal chamber is not for animals, nor for slaves, nor for defiled women — it is for free men and virgins.

**1:125** Through the Holy Spirit we are born again — and we are born through Christ in a twofold way. We are anointed through the Spirit. When we were born, we were united.

**1:126** No one will be able to see the bridal chamber without becoming a child of the bridal chamber. A Nazarene — "the one who reveals what is hidden." It is not possible for the son not to be born, and it is not possible for the [...] not to come.

**1:127** The holy man is entirely holy, down to his body itself. If he receives bread, he sanctifies it; if he receives a cup, or anything else — he purifies those too. And how could he not also purify his body?

---

**Council Notes (SOPHIA):**

*On the five sacraments:* The Gospel of Philip explicitly names five sacraments: baptism (vv. 28, 29, 43), chrism (vv. 33, 37, 110), eucharist (vv. 40, 49, 117), redemption (vv. 28, 29), and bridal chamber (vv. 28, 29, 87, 89, 91, 124–126). These are rendered with their technical terms consistently maintained across all translations, with "bridal chamber" retained as the established scholarly rendering of *nymphon*.

*On "companion" (koinonos):* In v. 51 and v. 119, Mary Magdalene is called the Savior's *koinonos* (companion/partner/consort). EMET and LOGOS render "companion"; PNEUMA renders "companion" — consensus holds "companion" as accurately representing the semantic range without over-determination.

*On the lacuna in the Mary Magdalene passage:* The manuscript is damaged at the crucial word — the body part kissed. All translations reflect this gap with [...] and do not supply "mouth" or any other word. This is non-negotiable scholarly practice.

*On duplicate passages:* Verses 50/118 and 51/119 are near-identical. Both are retained as the manuscript preserves them; this is an anthology characteristic, not a scribal error to be harmonized.

*On "Pharisath" (vv. 49, 117):* The etymology offered ("the one spread out / crucified") is a theological wordplay internal to the text, not a verifiable linguistic derivation. All translators render it as given, without endorsing its philological accuracy.

*On archon theology:* "Archons" is preserved untranslated in EMET; LOGOS and PNEUMA render contextually. SOPHIA preserves "archons" as the standard scholarly term for this Valentinian theological concept.

*On the restoration (apokatastasis):* Vv. 64 and 82 use *apokatastasis* — a term with significant patristic and Origenist resonance meaning universal restoration/restitution. All translations render "restoration" as the agreed English equivalent.

---
